title: Mild lip swelling after new antibiotic (borderline)
tricky_aspects: AI should list missing airway questions

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: My lip has swollen up a bit. I started penicillin yesterday for a throat infection.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: How old are you? When did the swelling start?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I'm 52. I noticed it maybe half an hour ago. Only the lower lip.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Any swelling of the tongue or throat, trouble swallowing or breathing, hoarse voice?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: No, I can swallow and breathe fine. My voice is normal.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Any rash, itching, dizziness or stomach pain?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: A few itchy red spots on my neck. No dizziness.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Have you taken a dose today?

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Don't take more penicillin. If you have an antihistamine you can take it now. A nurse will call you back to decide if you should come in. If your tongue or throat swells or breathing gets hard, call 112 immediately.
